prompt: In one town the longest day of the year has $16$ hours of daylight and the shortest has $8$ hours. Daylight through the year follows a sine wave. What is the AMPLITUDE, in hours?
hint: Amplitude is HALF the distance from the highest point to the lowest point.

hints.text: Amplitude is HALF the distance from the highest point to the lowest point.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Practise on an easier wave: it peaks at $10$ and dips to $2$. The gap is $8$, so the amplitude is $8 \div 2 = 4$. Now use the same two steps on $16$ and $8$.
The gap is $16 - 8 = 8$ hours. Halve it.

explanation: Check with the midline: the middle is $(16 + 8) \div 2 = 12$ h, and $12 + 4 = 16$, $12 - 4 = 8$. ✓

alternativeExplanations.title: Find the midline first
steps: The midline is the average of the two extremes: (16 + 8) ÷ 2 = 12 hours.
The amplitude is how far the peak sits above that midline: 16 − 12 = 4 hours.

alternativeExplanations.title: Build the equation
steps: Write daylight = a·sin(x) + k. Peak means k + a = 16; trough means k − a = 8.
Subtract the second from the first: 2a = 8, so a = 4 hours.
